issues.legal_issue: A declaration of acquisition cannot be published on the same date as the preliminary notification when the urgency procedure applies under the amended statutory scheme.
material_facts: The acquisition proceeded under the urgency provisions, and the usual objection procedure was dispensed with.
The preliminary notification and the acquisition declaration were issued and published on the same day.
The relevant amendment was in force when the acquisition proceedings took place.
issues.conclusion: The same-day declaration was invalid, and the appeals were dismissed, leaving the High Court's decision to quash it undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The amended wording of Section 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, permitting a declaration under Section 6 only after the date of publication of the notification under Section 4(1), requires a subsequent date even where urgency is invoked and the objection procedure is dispensed with. The Court applied the ordinary meaning of the words in the context and scheme of the Act, rather than speculate about unexpressed legislative purposes. Smt. Somawanti v. State of Punjab and Babu Singh v. Union of India had permitted simultaneous publication under the earlier wording; the Court found the amended language changed the position. It referred to Shri Balaganesan Metals v. M.R. Shanmugham Chetty and Raja Satyendra Narayan Singh v. State of Bihar on statutory construction, and considered Lord Howard de Walden v. IRC and Hopes v. Hopes on the significance of changed wording.

predicates.urgent_land_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns an acquisition of land in which the acquiring authority invokes an urgency procedure.
predicates.amended_text_requires_later_declaration: The governing text requires the acquisition declaration to follow the date of publication of the preliminary notification.
predicates.notification_and_declaration_published_s: The preliminary notification and acquisition declaration were published on the same date.

issues.definition: When an urgent land-acquisition proceeding is governed by text requiring the declaration to follow the preliminary notification, publishing both on the same date makes the declaration invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A fresh acquisition declaration may be issued after an invalid same-day declaration if the statutory period for making the declaration remains open.
material_facts: The declaration published on the same day as the preliminary notification was invalid.
The Court stated that a fresh declaration could be issued if the statutory period remained available.
issues.conclusion: The acquiring authority remained free to issue a fresh declaration within the period allowed by the applicable statutory time limit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that a fresh declaration under Section 6 could be issued within the period contemplated by the proviso to Section 6(1), read with its first Explanation, if the acquiring authority chose to do so.

predicates.land_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns a proposed acquisition of land requiring an acquisition declaration.
predicates.prior_declaration_invalid: An earlier acquisition declaration in the proceeding was held invalid.
predicates.statutory_declaration_period_open: The statutory period for making a valid acquisition declaration has not expired.

issues.definition: If an earlier declaration in a land-acquisition proceeding is invalid but the statutory period remains open, a fresh declaration may be issued.
